card.intuition: Output tokens are what the model generates back — the prose you read, the code it emits, tool calls, and any extended thinking done before answering. They are billed at a higher rate than input tokens, commonly around five times, because they cost more compute to produce. Output also sets the pace of a session, since it is generated one token at a time.
card.analogy: A luxury print shop that charges per printed page at five times the rate it charges to re-read your source file, and prints one character at a time — long custom prints are both slow and expensive.
card.time_complexity: The model reads input quickly but writes output one token at a time, so a slow turn usually means a long answer is coming; higher effort spends more output tokens before you see anything.
card.space_complexity: Output occupies its own side of the token budget — reasoning tokens are billed even when the harness hides them, so an unseen thinking phase still eats the window and the bill.
when_to_use: Explaining why hidden reasoning tokens still appear on the bill
Cutting costs by getting an agent to emit small edits instead of rewriting whole files
Diagnosing a slow turn — the long wait usually means long output being written
gotchas: Reasoning tokens count as output even when the harness never shows them to you
Rewriting whole files instead of patching burns credit, since output costs about five times the input rate

exercise.prompt: Output tokens are billed at five times the input rate. Write request_cost that returns a single request's total given its input and output token counts.
exercise.starter_code:
INPUT_RATE = 1
OUTPUT_RATE = 5

def request_cost(in_tokens, out_tokens):
    return in_tokens * INPUT_RATE + out_tokens * ___________
hints: Multiply the output count by its premium rate constant
The total is the input charge plus the output charge
